full_judgment:
The appellants herein as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.56 of 1983 for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction in respect of the land described in the second schedule of the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Ranjit Kumar Kar and his three brothers in Mourashi Maliki right. Rashid Ali had been possessing the land as a tenant under them on payment of rent since 1941. Subsequently, Rashid Ali purchased the entire second schedule land from Ranjit Kumar Kar and others for valuable consideration by a registered deed of sale dated 28th Magh, 1359 BS corresponding to 11-2-1953. Rashid Ali, being the owner in possession of the first schedule land, sold it to the plaintiffs by a registered deed of sale dated 8th Chaitra, 1372 BS corresponding to 22-3-1966. The plaintiffs have since been possessing and enjoying the first schedule land, living in the homestead portion of the suit property with family members and growing and planting trees, vegetables in the vhita land. The plaintiffs have been possessing the entire first schedule land for more than 12 years to the knowledge of all defendants and others and thus acquired title thereto by adverse possession. In the third week of November, 1982 defendant Nos. 1 to 4 claimed title to and interest in the first schedule land [attracted by Sylhet Survey (SS) Plot No. 3428 and 3432] and gave out threat that they would soon take forcible possession thereof. Soon after, the plaintiffs made search in the Sub-Registrar's office and found that defendant Nos.1-4 created a fraudulent and collusive deed of sale dated 28-2-1974 in respect of the SS Plot Nos. 3428 and 3432 of the first schedule land. The said deed was alleged to have been executed by defendant No.6, Jamini Kumar Kar, through his alleged attorney Arun Chowdhury. Jamini Kumar Kar had no right, title and interest in the land of SS plot Nos. 3428 and 3432. The deed of sale and the power of attorney in favour of Arun Chowdhury are false, fraudulent and collusive. During S.A. operation, the land of first schedule was recorded in three SS plots, namely, plot Nos. 3433, 3428 and 3432; SS plot Nos. 3428 and 3432 were wrongly recorded in the names of Sachindra Kar and Jamini Mohan Kar (defendant Nos.5 and 6 respectively) and the other SS plot No.3433 was recorded in the name of Rashid Ali (vendor of the plaintiffs) and Harendra Kumar Kar in equal share. The defendants are not in possession of any portion of the first schedule land attracted by the aforesaid two plots. Taking advantage of the wrong recording of the suit property in SA Khatian, defendant Nos. 1 to 4 collusively created fraudulent documents to lay claim of title to the first schedule property to the extent of land measuring 4.20 acres. Hence the plaintiffs filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. l to 4 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in brief, is that SS plot No. 3433 appertaining to Khatian Nos.1348 and 112 belonged to Sikandar Ali and others and they have been in actual possession on the northern part thereof. Neither the plaintiffs nor their vendor Rashid Ali had any interest and possession in the land of SS plot No. 3433. The description of land of both the schedules in the plaint is vague, indefinite and imaginary. The land of the second schedule does not fall within the land of first schedule. In other words, the land of first schedule is not attracted by the land of SS Plot Nos. 3433, 3432 and 3428 originally belonging to defendant Nos.5(Srish) and defendant No.6 (Jamini). To tie knowledge of all concerned, the SA record of rights was prepared correctly in their names in respect of plots Nos. 4332 and 3428 without any objection from any quarter. By an amicable arrangement, Jamini Kar, defendant No.6, got the entire land of SS 3432 and 3428. Defendant No.6 Jamini Kar through his appointed attorney (Arun Chowdhury) sold 4.20 acres of land to defendant Nos. 1 to 4 by a registered deed of sale dated 28-2-1974 AD and delivered possession thereof to them. Defendant Nos. 1 to 4 transferred 60 decimals of land of SS plot No.3428 along with other lands to one Muzahid Ali by a deed of sale dated 12- 3-1974 who, in his turn, transferred the said 60 decimals to Makbul Ali, son of defendant No.3 (Mustakim Ali) by a registered deed of sale. In the aforesaid manner defendant Nos. 1 to 4 and Mukbul Ali have been possessing their respective shares of the suit property. Defendants Nos. 1 to 4 .got their names recorded in record of right in respect of 4.20 acres of land of SS Plot No.3428 and 3432 and they have also paid rent therefore. The plaintiffs have got no right or title to the suit land' and as such prayed for dismissal of the suit. Defendant No.15 also filed a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and claimed to have purchased 0.90 acre of land of SS Plot No.3428 from defendant No.3, Makbul Ali, on the basis of 3(three) registered deeds of sale in the year 1982 and since then he has been in possession of his portion of the suit property and as such prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 22. The findings of the High Court Division that the plaintiffs could not prove the title of their predecessor-in-interest, Rashid Ali pursuant to Exhibit-1 in the first schedule land by other documentary evidence such as rent receipts to show payment of rent by Rashid Ali to the Government after S.A. operation. The aforesaid finding is erroneous because mere non-payment of rent does not affect the title accrued through lawful transfer admittedly when the title of Ranjit Kar and his brother from whom Rashid Ali purchased the suit land was not denied. In addition, SS plot No.3433 was recorded in the name of plaintiffs vendor, Rashid Ali in the SA khatian in respect of 1.11 acres of land. Therefore, the title of plaintiffs vendor has been well established in the aforesaid 1.11 acres of land. So far the deed of sale dated 22-3-1966 (Exhibit 1Ka) is concerned it appears that the deed could not be proved according to the requirement of section 67 of the Evidence Act. Since the contesting defendants do not have any claim over the land of plot No.3433 and since the title of plaintiffs' vendor in 1.11 acres of land of that plot IS established we are of the view that the suit may be decreed in part so far as it relates to 1.11 acres of land of suit plot No.3433 shown in the second schedule to the plaint. However, we are of the view that the plaintiffs could not prove their title in respect of SS Plot Nos. 3428 and 3432 in accordance with law.
